# Decision

<!-- Generated by decision 0.9.0. Edit the generator in rolandkakonyi/decision. -->

Use the installed `decision` command or its MCP `evaluate` tool for typed
judgments over explicitly selected context. A Noul returns a yes probability;
a Choice selects one named option with probabilities; a Score evaluates ordered
rubric levels. Box questions locate an object in an image with TypeSafe/Jev;
OpenAI/Gemini Decisions and Cloudflare Clef support Noul, Choice, and Score. The harness accepts
JSON state and PNG/JPEG images. It produces data rather than
prose explanations or researched answers. Keep policy and actions in code.

## Prerequisites

Run `decision --version` to confirm installation. This skill does not include
the executable. Install it separately from the
[decision repository](https://github.com/rolandkakonyi/decision), either as a
standalone executable or with `uv tool install /path/to/decision`. See its
[build guide](https://github.com/rolandkakonyi/decision/blob/main/docs/standalone.md).
Do not silently install or change the user's MCP settings as part of a query.
To package this skill as a Codex plugin, use `decision plugin --output DIR`
with `--integration cli` or `--integration mcp` (default). Read
`references/plugin.md` for local installation, executable selection, environment
forwarding, refresh, and `--check` instructions. Generation does not install it.

## Multiple questions, one provider request

Resolve `references/request.json` relative to this SKILL.md as a mixed-question
example. It contains a shared `state` and a `questions` object keyed by question
IDs. Each question has `type`, `instructions`, and any `criteria`.

```bash
decision run /private/request.json --dry-run
decision run /private/request.json
decision run /private/request.json --json
decision ask --state-file /private/state.json --questions-file /private/questions.json
decision ask --state 'Please refund my payment.' --questions-file - < /private/questions.json
```

Questions sharing state are sent together in ONE provider request; answers keep
their IDs. Each question is independent and cannot see other answers. Use a
later request when its inputs depend on an earlier answer. Only one file input
may consume stdin (`-`) in each invocation. Missing, unexpected, or incorrectly
typed answers fail explicitly instead of becoming a partial batch.

## Single questions

```bash
decision noul 'Does the message request a refund?' --state 'Please refund this.'
decision choice 'Which team handles this?' --state-file /private/state.json \
  --option billing='Payments and refunds' --option technical='Bugs and integrations'
decision score 'How blocked is the customer?' --state 'The app crashes on launch.' \
  --level 'Can proceed' --level 'Needs a workaround' --level 'Cannot proceed'
```

`--state` supplies literal text; `--state-file` supplies a JSON value or reads
stdin with `-`. Images can supply state on their own. `--dry-run` validates and
previews the request without API access. Output contains the selected context
and should be handled accordingly. CLI output is human-readable by default;
use `--json` (before or after the query command) for structured answers, model,
and usage. Use `--dry-run --json` for a JSON request preview. Scripts must opt
in to JSON from version 0.4.0 onward. Diagnostics go to stderr. Exit
codes: 0 success/dry run, 1 provider failure, 2 invalid input/missing credentials,
130 interruption. A failure is never a negative judgment. The default timeout
is 30 seconds, and requests are not automatically retried.

Every successful CLI/MCP evaluation includes `usage.input_tokens`,
`usage.output_tokens`, and `duration_ms`. Readable CLI output always shows token
counts and duration. Unreported token counts are `null` in JSON/MCP and shown
as unavailable in readable output; zero remains zero. Duration uses a monotonic
clock around SDK setup, image upload, and provider response handling. Stats
cover the entire batch, excluding process startup and local file validation.
Dry runs have no response stats because no provider request is sent.

## Images and Box

```bash
decision choice 'Which breed is the dog in images.dog?' \
  --image dog=dog.jpg --model jev-1.14.0 \
  --option french_bulldog='French bulldog' --option english_bulldog='English bulldog'
decision noul 'Is the dog in images.dog a French bulldog?' --image dog=dog.jpg --model jev-1.14.0
decision box 'Locate the dog in images.dog' --image dog=dog.jpg --model jev-1.14.0
```

Read `references/examples.md` for worked Choice, Noul, Score, Box, `ask`, and
`run` examples. The option key before `=` is returned in a Choice answer; the
text after `=` describes it. A Choice selects one of the offered options.
For Noul, Box, and Choice together, use `references/dog-mixed-questions.json`
with `ask`, or `references/dog-mixed-request.json` with `run`. The worked guide
also shows the equivalent MCP `evaluate` input.

Repeat `--image [NAME=]PATH` for several images. Unnamed images are called
`image`, `image_2`, and so on. Flag images are attached under `state.images`;
existing object fields are preserved, while scalar state is placed in
`state.context`. Questions can refer to `images.door`. Duplicate names or an
existing non-object `state.images` fail rather than being overwritten.

Batch JSON can also include `assets`, keyed by a unique reference such as
`<photo>`, with descriptors `{"path": "photo.png"}` or
`{"data_base64": "...", "format": "png"}`. Use that reference in state,
instructions, or criteria; object keys do not count as references. See
`references/images.json` for a CLI template requiring your own image. Paths in
a request file are relative to that file; paths in stdin or flags are relative
to the working directory. Every asset must be referenced. Each image is sent
once per batch, even when several questions share it: TypeSafe uses multipart
uploads; OpenAI and Cloudflare use base64 data URLs.

MCP accepts only `data_base64` assets, never local file paths. Base64 must use
the standard alphabet without whitespace or a data: prefix. Optional `type`
must be `image`; format can be png, jpg, or jpeg. Format is inferred when omitted.
Prefer the shared state for an image used by several questions.

In TypeSafe mode, the harness automatically sets the required
`TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images: true` header for images or Box. TypeSafe currently
labels images/Box experimental. Box needs Jev 1.14; use `--model jev-1.14.0`
or another compatible model. Local checks enforce PNG/JPEG signatures and
16 MiB per file / 32 MiB combined; the provider enforces decoding, dimensions,
and expanded-request limits. Current TypeSafe images must be 280-1568 pixels
on each side and are never resized by this CLI. Check the
[image docs](https://docs.typesafe.ai/images) when limits change.

## Provider configuration

- `--provider` overrides `DECISION_PROVIDER`: `typesafe` (default), `openai`, `cloudflare`, `gemini`, or an installed provider extension.
- `--base-url` overrides `DECISION_BASE_URL`, then the selected provider's
  `TYPESAFE_BASE_URL`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL`, `CLOUDFLARE_BASE_URL`, or `GEMINI_BASE_URL`.
  Defaults are `https://api.typesafe.ai`, `https://api.openai.com/v1`,
  `https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4`, and
  `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta`. Include the API prefix.
- `--api-key-env MY_PROVIDER_KEY` overrides `DECISION_API_KEY_ENV`, selecting an
  environment variable by name. Without a selector, use `DECISION_API_KEY`.
- Only the matching provider's official HTTPS host can fall back to
  `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` / `TYPESAFEAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, or
  `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` / `CLOUDFLARE_AUTH_TOKEN`, or
  `GEMINI_API_KEY` / `GOOGLE_API_KEY` (in that order). Other hosts
  require an explicitly selected provider key. Keys never cross providers implicitly.
- `--model` overrides `DECISION_MODEL`, then the CLI request's model. Without a
  selected model, TypeSafe uses `TYPESAFE_DEFAULT_MODEL` or its SDK default,
  while OpenAI uses `gpt-6-luna`, Cloudflare uses `clef`, and Gemini uses `gemini-decision-1`.
  MCP per-call model overrides its server default.

- Cloudflare's `--account-id` overrides `DECISION_ACCOUNT_ID`, then
  `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`. The default API root requires an account ID;
  a custom Cloudflare base URL must be a Workers AI run root, such as
  `https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/ACCOUNT_ID/ai/run`.
  The adapter appends `/@cf/cloudflare/clef` or `/@cf/cloudflare/clef-flash`.
- HTTPS is required except on local loopback. Other providers must implement
  the selected System One or Decisions contract; a chat-completions endpoint
  is insufficient. Env files are not loaded automatically.

External providers require installation in the same Python environment as
`decision`; standalone executables support built-ins only. Providers are trusted
Python code. Select the registered name with `--provider NAME` or
`DECISION_PROVIDER`. Extensions share common request/result validation, credential
host restrictions, and fixed MCP routing. Generated skills and Codex plugin
exports never discover or execute external providers. Forward custom credential
variable names with `decision plugin --env-var NAME` for MCP integration.

```bash
export DECISION_BASE_URL=https://provider.example/api
export DECISION_API_KEY_ENV=OTHER_PROVIDER_KEY
export DECISION_MODEL=provider-model
decision run /private/request.json
```

Keys are resolved from the environment, never command-line values. Send only
context authorized for the selected provider. Do not forward entire repositories,
chat histories, or secrets implicitly, or substitute providers after a failure.
For experiments, establish the data and budget first. Provider access still
depends on the execution environment's network settings.

For OpenAI, use `--provider openai --model gpt-6-luna`. Noul is translated to
native `predicate`; Choice criteria become named choices and Score criteria
become ordered levels. Common answer IDs/types and stats stay the same.
Objects and arrays of objects are passed as `input_json`; other state values
are text. Images use shared base64 data URLs with reference labels. Structured
criterion descriptions are JSON text; Noul criteria are included in instructions.
The API supports 1–400 questions, 2–255 choices, and 2–10 score levels. Box
is rejected before sending any request. Refusals or malformed answers fail the
whole batch without partial judgments. Read `references/examples.md` and use
`references/openai-dog-questions.json` or `references/openai-dog-request.json`.
See the [official Decisions guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/decisions).

For Cloudflare Workers AI, use `--provider cloudflare` with `--model clef`
(default) or `--model clef-flash`. Full `@cf/cloudflare/` model IDs are also
accepted. Export `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` (Workers AI token template; custom
tokens require Workers AI Read and Edit permissions) and
`CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` for the official endpoint. Noul, Choice, and Score
use the shared format, including mixed batches, images, and response stats.
Box is rejected before any request. Limits are 1–64 questions, IDs containing
1–100 letters/digits/underscores/dots/hyphens, 2–255 choices, 2–10 score levels,
and 4 PNG/JPEG images: 4 MiB each, 8 MiB combined, 13 MiB encoded request body.
The provider enforces image decoding and 16-megapixel dimensions. Images are
sent in asset order; the adapter adds `state._decision_image_references` to
map asset names to 1-based image positions. This field is reserved for image
requests; scalar state is preserved under `context`. Unsuccessful envelopes,
malformed answers, and incomplete batches fail without partial judgments.
Use `references/cloudflare-dog-questions.json` or
`references/cloudflare-dog-request.json`; see the worked guide and
[official Clef docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/models/clef/).

For Gemini, use `--provider gemini` with `GEMINI_API_KEY` exported. The default
model is `gemini-decision-1`. JSON state is serialized as text; named PNG/JPEG
images are sent once as inline base64 content blocks with reference labels.
Common Noul criteria `true`/`false` map to `true_description`/`false_description`;
structured descriptions become JSON text and absent Choice descriptions become
empty strings. Limits are 1–1000 questions, IDs of 1–64 ASCII letters, digits,
underscores, or hyphens, 2–255 choices, and 2–255 nonempty score levels.
Option IDs allow 1–128 characters, internal ASCII spaces, and no edge spaces,
control characters, or non-ASCII spaces. The harness retains its 16 MiB per-image
and 32 MiB combined limits; Gemini enforces its context and media limits.
Box is rejected locally. Audio, video, and PDFs are not accepted by this harness.
Gemini usage is normalized to input/output tokens; zero output counts stay zero.
Malformed, blocked, or incomplete batches return no judgments. Use
`references/gemini-dog-questions.json` or `references/gemini-dog-request.json`;
see the [official Decisions guide](https://aistudio.google.com/docs/decisions-api).

## MCP and code mode

`decision mcp` serves one STDIO tool, `evaluate({state, questions, model?, assets?})`.
Prefer this tool when available for structured code-mode composition. Named
questions share one request just as in the CLI. Success returns
`structuredContent` with answers, model, usage, and `duration_ms`, with a declared output schema;
failures set `isError` and return no answer. MCP remains structured regardless
of the CLI output default. Stdout is reserved for MCP protocol
messages. Provider, base URL, account ID, key selection, and timeout remain server configuration, and
the tool's optional model overrides the server default.

When setting up MCP explicitly:

```bash
codex mcp add decision -- /absolute/path/to/decision mcp
codex mcp add decision-openai -- /absolute/path/to/decision mcp --provider openai
codex mcp add decision-cloudflare -- /absolute/path/to/decision mcp --provider cloudflare
codex mcp add decision-gemini -- /absolute/path/to/decision mcp --provider gemini
```

Forward both the selector and the selected credential variable, for example
`DECISION_API_KEY_ENV` and `OTHER_PROVIDER_KEY`, plus any provider/model settings
in the server's `env_vars` configuration. For TypeSafe, forward
`TYPESAFE_API_KEY` or `TYPESAFEAI_API_KEY` instead; for OpenAI, forward `OPENAI_API_KEY`.
For Cloudflare, forward `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`.
OpenAI and Cloudflare servers advertise only their supported types and provider limits.
Cancellation cannot undo an
already-sent provider request; its timeout still bounds it.
